elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained sentence: "This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions." New York is the preferred governing law; the conflicts carve-out is unchanged.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York will have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement, provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." Both state and federal courts in New York County are named, exclusivity is tied to the merits, and the only alternate-forum carve-out is the customary temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The operative language selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not met at the fallback level, but irrelevant because the preferred level is fully satisfied.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum is New York County courts, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Again immaterial because the redline achieves the preferred position.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York substantive law is retained and a single inserted sentence supplies exclusive merits jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County.
The temporary injunctive relief carve-out is the customary narrow exception and does not undercut the exclusive merits forum; no broader alternate forum or arbitration seat is introduced.

Minimal: the existing governing-law sentence is untouched word for word, no favourable language is deleted, and only the missing forum sentence is added. A concise insertion for a wholly absent forum provision is permissible even though all its words are new; no survival tails, fee-shifting, procedures, or other extras were appended.

Preserves intent: no defined terms, cross-references, or commercial mechanics are disturbed; the conflict-of-laws exclusion survives and there is no contradictory retained dispute-resolution or arbitration clause elsewhere in the document per the drafter's search, which the cited paragraphs corroborate.

Finding status of "deviation" is appropriate: the absence of any forum provision means the clause failed the venue half of both the preferred and the fallback positions, so a redline rather than a rationale note was warranted.
